page.title: Core Application
page.summary: The core application is a Meteor monolith containing 4735 source files organized into 6 architectural layers. It runs as an isomorphic JavaScript application with separate client and server entry points, serving as the foundation for 15 major feature subsystems that handle everything from omnichannel communication to admin functions.

prose.text:
The core application is the Meteor monolith at `apps/meteor` — 4735 source files organized into 6 layers:

| Layer | Files | Role |
|---|---:|---|
| `apps/meteor/client/` | 2854 | Client SPA (React frontend) |
| `apps/meteor/app/` | 1077 | Shared Meteor packages (client + server) |
| `apps/meteor/server/` | 416 | Meteor server runtime |
| `apps/meteor/ee/` | 290 | Enterprise Edition overrides |
| `apps/meteor/lib/` | 56 | Shared isomorphic library |
| `apps/meteor/definition/` | 42 | Ambient type definitions |

Sources: apps/meteor/package.json:1
prose.narrative: The codebase is divided into six layers with distinct responsibilities. The client layer contains 2854 files implementing a React single-page application, while the server layer has 416 files for Meteor runtime logic. Shared code lives in the app layer (1077 files) for code that runs on both sides, with enterprise-specific overrides isolated in the ee layer (290 files). Isomorphic utilities occupy the lib layer (56 files) and type definitions are centralized in the definition layer (42 files).

prose.text:
The app boots from two entry points (client + server halves of the isomorphic Meteor app):

- `apps/meteor/server/main.ts`
- `apps/meteor/client/main.ts`

Sources: apps/meteor/server/main.ts:1, apps/meteor/client/main.ts:1
prose.narrative: The application boots from two separate entry point files: one for the server runtime and one for the client frontend. These define where the Meteor framework initializes and loads the respective halves of the isomorphic application.

prose.text:
The largest feature subsystems living inside the core app (by file count; `fanIn` = how much the rest of the system depends on them):

| Subsystem | Files (in app) | fanIn |
|---|---:|---:|
| `omnichannel` | 466 | 3897 |
| `room` | 432 | 8061 |
| `admin` | 397 | 133 |
| `components` | 304 | 922 |
| `marketplace` | 175 | 830 |
| `api` | 169 | 129 |
| `livechat` | 148 | 1387 |
| `utils` | 126 | 3375 |
| `hooks` | 124 | 752 |
| `livechat-enterprise` | 98 | 1118 |
| `root` | 78 | 841 |
| `settings` | 72 | 3664 |
| `navbar` | 65 | 522 |
| `app:functions` | 64 | 202 |
| `navigation` | 64 | 266 |
prose.narrative: The largest subsystems by file count are omnichannel (466 files) and room (432 files), though the room subsystem has significantly higher fan-in (8061 references), meaning other parts of the system depend heavily on it. Utility subsystems like utils, settings, and hooks are heavily reused (fan-in 3375, 3664, and 752 respectively) despite having fewer files. Smaller feature areas like admin (397 files) and components (304 files) serve more specialized purposes with lower dependency counts.
